purpose: Candidate Beamer renderer work derived from manual real-world review; observed gaps and integration tasks, not a declaration that all primitives are unimplemented.
policy: Built-in Beamer and defined interfaces of established packages qualify even when concentrated in one author collection.
Source frequency helps prioritize broad mechanisms; this corpus is not a package-popularity survey.
Expand supported author definitions generically; do not hardcode macro/environment names.
A mixed-case failure does not prove each nested primitive is unsupported. Isolate causes before implementation.

summary.selection: Purposive feature-diverse manual sample, not a corpus pass-rate estimate. Source excerpts, native rasters and corresponding TeX rasters inspected; continuation and overprint strips inspected separately.

countLimitations: Frequency counts only complete scanner-discovered environment frames. Command/macro-generated and recovery spans can be missed.
Frequency is source usage, not rendering support. Package presence alone does not count as use.
Exact repeated frame source is deduplicated per repository; semantic duplicates and generated variants can remain.
Inputs are expanded conservatively; conditionals, package definitions and custom build wrappers are not executed.
Repository diversity here covers eight source collections, not population-wide package popularity.

todos.title: Preserve nested flow and block bodies
todos.task: Keep supported prose, lists, equations and assets inside columns/blocks/lists. Confine an unsupported child to its smallest source-backed boundary; do not drop siblings or silently keep only a block heading.

evidence.observation: Native resolves and paints the picture, but splits the containing enumerate/columns sequence into placeholders and loses the matrix block/table. The block title group is omitted in this source; use the valid block examples elsewhere for a general block-body regression.

A leading footnote with a URL is followed by two ordinary lists. Native replaces all of this with one unsupported box. TeX renders the lists and email footnote. Fallback should be confined to the unsupported leaf.

This valid empty-title exampleblock contains a formula, followed by built-in overprint with five unbraced onslide alternatives including handout selectors. TeX renders five states; native discovers one, loses the block formula and substitutes an overprint placeholder.

Native discovers both pause states but replaces the initial prose/list with one unsupported box on each. At step two the block heading appears without its aligned one-hot vectors. TeX renders both prose and matrix block.

An ordinary nested list contains equations, cases and a source-declared diag operator. Native replaces the whole body with a placeholder. Test declared math operators and nested flow separately before assigning a precise cause; do not add a hardcoded diag shortcut.

The exampleblock title survives, but both its explanatory inline math and lstlisting with math escapes disappear. Native records zero literal fallbacks and zero unsupported layout items. TeX renders the complete body. This demonstrates a paint/content-coverage blind spot in automatic triage.

todos.title: Render tables in slide flow
todos.task: Start with tabular alignment, row breaks, rules and booktabs, then paragraph columns, multicolumn and mixed math/text. Exercise direct, column-contained and scaled tables.

evidence.observation: TeX splits this source frame into three continuation pages: diagram, table, then reduction formula and links. Native flattens them into one clipped slide. Basic TikZ geometry survives; node fonts and positioning need calibration after flow is fixed.

TeX has three continuation pages, including nested/scaled tables and matrices; native shows five placeholders on one slide. Some block environments omit the required title group: do not make that source irregularity a supported syntax requirement. The ordinary tables and allowframebreaks still provide clear general evidence.

The center column uses basic tabular and booktabs; native prints its syntax instead of laying out rows. The wideitemize wrapper on the left is an author macro/environment and should be addressed through generic definition expansion.

A standard confusion matrix uses tabular, rules and rotatebox for a header. Native replaces the whole table with a placeholder; TeX renders rows and the rotated label. No author-specific construct is needed to explain this gap.
The heading and texttt call survive. A simple two-column tabular becomes a placeholder and def arraystretch is printed literally. TeX renders the rows with larger spacing and typography.

The dense table uses array m columns, parbox, small text and shrink. Native replaces it and the references with placeholders. The mytitle and emoji aliases are author constructs; supporting table/paragraph/scale mechanisms has general value. Shrink itself needs a minimal fixture once body layout works.

avoidAuthorSpecificFeatures: Dedicated wideitemize, BI/BIL, myboxtitle, Procedure, slidecore or items implementations. Use source-defined expansion or preserve a local fallback.
Custom mytitle/emoji/math-name aliases and removelatexerror hacks.
Custom bus-system, confusion-matrix or crowdsourcing-diagram special cases; fix common flow/graphics/math mechanisms.
Unbounded author theme/template execution and private institutional style packages.
automaticFollowups: Current shortlist uses token-aware family detection, exact-source deduplication and repository/deck diversity caps. Optional rendering reports text-engine literals, unsupported flow, missing-asset suspicions and diagnostic omissions.
Add paint-aware source coverage so an empty block body such as r2-43 is flagged. A layout record alone does not prove paint.
Compare state and continuation-page counts after valid reference compilation; gate numerical comparisons on explicit correspondence.
Use component-level or ink-weighted raster comparisons once fonts/context are controlled; whole-slide white-space RMSE can hide missing material.
Keep direct-asset, ordinary block/math and item-overlay controls alongside failure candidates; some clean results must remain in manual sampling.

conformanceSuite.policy: Use the existing exact glyph/font/geometry gates. Current failures remain red; count mismatches withhold glyph comparisons. alltt/lstlisting require recognition and supported sibling preservation, not code typesetting.
